title: 1977 AHSME Problem 21
statement: For how many values of the coefficient \(a\) do the equations \[ \begin{aligned} x^2+ax+1&=0,\\ x^2-x-a&=0 \end{aligned} \] have a common real solution?

solutions.text:
Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \[ \begin{gathered} (a+1)x+(a+1)\\ =(a+1)(x+1)=0. \end{gathered} \] If \(a=-1,\) the common equation is \(x^2-x+1=0,\) which has no real roots. Otherwise \(x=-1,\) and substitution into \(x^2-x-a=0\) gives \(a=2.\) This value works, so exactly one value of \(a\) qualifies.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
